label: Custom / manual
notes: No auto-fill. Set Direct API format and Direct API URL yourself.

label: Ollama
notes: Exposes both a native /api/* surface and an OpenAI-compatible /v1/* shim (chat/completions, completions, embeddings, models). No /v1/responses. Unloading is a parameter on /api/generate or /api/chat, not a separate endpoint.

endpoints.description: OpenAI-compatible chat completions (used by this pack's "openai" Direct API format).
OpenAI-compatible text completions.
OpenAI-compatible embeddings.
OpenAI-compatible model list.
Native single-prompt generation. Send {"keep_alive": 0} with the model name to unload it immediately after the call.
Native multi-turn chat. Also accepts {"keep_alive": 0} to unload after the call.
Native embeddings (current).
Native embeddings (legacy alias of /api/embed).
List models available locally.
List models currently loaded in memory, with VRAM usage.

label: LM Studio
notes: Exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints (including /v1/responses), an Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages endpoint (not implemented by this pack), and its own /api/v0 (documented) and /api/v1 (used live in earlier testing, not fully documented) REST surfaces for model management.

endpoints.description: OpenAI-compatible chat completions.
OpenAI-compatible text completions.
OpenAI-compatible embeddings.
OpenAI-compatible model list.
OpenAI Responses-shaped endpoint (this pack's "responses" Direct API format; not the default preset choice here).
Anthropic Messages-compatible endpoint. Not implemented by this pack's request-building code.
Native REST v1 model list, used to find a loaded model's instance_id for unload. Confirmed by live testing, not fully covered in current official docs.
Native REST v1 unload. Body is {"instance_id": ...} (NOT {"model": ...} - that 400s). Confirmed by live testing, not fully covered in current official docs.

label: llama.cpp server
notes: Exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints (including /v1/responses, which converts to its chat pipeline internally) plus a native completion/utility surface. No documented model-unload endpoint (a server instance is normally started against one already-loaded model).

label: vLLM
notes: Exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints; newer releases also add /v1/responses (stateful, tool-calling), but this preset keeps Chat Completions as the safer default since Responses support varies by version. No standard model-unload endpoint (vLLM is normally deployed against one fixed model).

endpoints.description: OpenAI-compatible chat completions - the recommended default.
OpenAI-compatible text completions. vLLM's own docs call this endpoint legacy.
OpenAI-compatible embeddings (embedding models only).
OpenAI-compatible model list.
Newer, stateful Responses-shaped endpoint with built-in tool support. Availability depends on the vLLM version.
Tokenize text (any model with a tokenizer).
Convert token IDs back to text.
Raw pooling output (pooling models).
Relevance scoring (cross-encoder / embedding models).
Health check.

label: Unsloth Studio
notes: Exposes /v1/chat/completions, an OpenAI Responses-shaped /v1/responses, and an Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages (not implemented by this pack) - all require an Authorization: Bearer sk-unsloth-... key generated in Settings -> API. /v1/load and /v1/unload are reported in Unsloth's own GitHub issues but are not on its primary API docs page; treat them as less certain than the endpoints above. Default port may vary by install -- check your own configuration if this preset's URL doesn't match.

endpoints.description: OpenAI-compatible chat completions. Supports streaming, tool calling, and vision.
OpenAI Responses-shaped endpoint (this pack's "responses" Direct API format).
Anthropic Messages-compatible endpoint, for Claude-Code-style clients. Not implemented by this pack's request-building code.
List currently loaded models.
Load a model by model_path. Documented in GitHub issues, not the primary API docs; the request does not respond until loading finishes, which can take minutes for large models.
Unload a model by model_path. Same sourcing caveat as /v1/load.
